matchups.recap:
The Chair Force put together a decent flight plan with Trevor Lawrence going off for 26.1 and Trey McBride chipping in 20.0, but George Pickens turned into a stunned naval battle queen at 4.3 and J.K. Dobbins ate his trail cheese and salami for a Beak 3.6 that never got going. Two of your marquee names walked on the alpine vegetation in Week 1, and that's the kind of game plan that gets you a loss instead of sticky buns on Sunday Morning.

Lone Eagle had a feel for the matchup from the jump, riding Justin Jefferson's 27.2 and Lamar Jackson's 24.96 like they were the whole scheme. Aaron Jones Sr. added a Boss 10.0, and with almost nothing wasted on the bench, this was about as clean a coaching job as Week 1 allows. It wasn't a Pioneer in Gaga ball blowout, more a hard-fought tug of war, but the Lone Eagle out-prepared the Chair Force from snap one and banked the well-earned Tuna Casserole.

away.name: Chase Brown Had a Bad Scare

matchups.recap:
Harley Jarvis put together the biggest smackdown of Week 1, and even with Tony Pollard turning in a Dutch Oven-adjacent 3.9 and Ja'Marr Chase mailing in 2.2, none of it mattered. Ashton Jeanty ran like a woodsman running to the camp store on his way to 29.7, David Montgomery chipped in 27.4, and Jalen Hurts added 24.72 to carry the load like a Woodsman Chief on a hike. The 143.02 was overkill, and for a 57.68-point post hike scrub, I want you to BRING DOWN THE ROOF.

Chase Brown Had a Bad Scare never had an answer. Chris Olave's 23.2 and Jared Goff's 16.44 were the only things resembling a game plan, while Drake London and Marvin Harrison Jr. combined to look Stuck in the Sewards at 4.5 and 3.8. This offense Had their lunch eaten by Yellow Yellow all afternoon, finishing at 85.34 with zero feel for the matchup and even less firepower to answer Harley Jarvis's Penis Eating Pike of a roster.

Old Balls opened the season with a game plan that had a feel for the matchup, riding Jaxon Smith-Njigba's 22.2 and the Steelers D/ST's 19.0 to a Bust Hike over The Machine Knows. Breece Hall chipped in 18.8, and Funk that Junk had enough arrows near the bullseye to survive a slow build and grind out a win that never quite felt safe until the final whistle.

The Machine Knows leaned entirely on Josh Allen's 35.66 to keep this competitive, and for a while it looked like enough. But Rico Dowdle Walked on the alpine vegetation all afternoon, turning a projected 11.65 into a Beak 3.1 and leaving the offense limping. Javonte Williams put up a Boss 21.7, Matthew Golden was fine at 12.5, but the coaching never adjusted to Dowdle's disappearing act, and the Preseason Power Rankings #1 opens the year 0-1 by 4.06.

Paralegal opened the season with a game plan that had all the arrows in the bullseye, letting D'Andre Swift and Jahmyr Gibbs carry the load like a Woodsman Chief on a hike, both clearing 30 points like it was nothing. A.J. Brown was the lone Beak note, stuck at 4.1 on an 11.54 projection, but with that kind of Boss backfield production it barely mattered. 55 Burgers cruised to a post hike scrub of a win, and Counsel didn't need to sweat a single Sunday snap.

Chef Boyardee, or however Stephanowitz spells it this week, got a Boss floor from Jonathan Taylor's 23.6 and a sneaky-Boss Seahawks defense, but Terry McLaurin was an absolute non-factor at 2.4 and dragged the whole receiving corps down with him. The Goose is Loose looked like it was bushwhacking without a compass for most of the afternoon, out-schemed from the jump, and a 32.66-point beatdown is exactly what happens when your game plan can't keep pace with someone else's.
Team Bradford beat Love Thy Naber 108.84-58.4. Top scorer: Derrick Henry with 34.8.

Week 1 and The Island Gudge already looks like the team nobody wants to see in November. 46er got Kenneth Walker III going for 32.6 and Christian Watson chipping in 29.7, and even Quinshon Judkins mailing in a 6.0 against a 12.2 projection couldn't slow the post hike scrub down. This is a manager who understands matchups before anyone else has finished their coffee, and a 54-point margin in Week 1 is the Gudge simply reminding the league who runs this thing.

Ricky Huns, meanwhile, spent the afternoon Bushwhacking without a compass despite Jaxson Dart quietly going off for 26.6. Ladd McConkey and Kyren Williams did their part too, but none of it mattered because the game plan around them never had a chance against a Boss roster clicking on every cylinder. Other Nate will look back at this one and see a team that competed in spurts but never found the answers it needed, Beak decisions compounding into a laugher by the fourth quarter.

headline: Rome-ans edge Wine Mixon as Love Thy Naber gets crushed
